2611.32138.title: VIDE : Training-Free Video Anomaly Detection via Visual Intrinsic Distribution Estimation

2611.32274.abstract: Solving nonlinear partial differential equations (PDEs) over long time horizons is computationally expensive using traditional numerical methods. While neural operators provide an efficient alternative, they suffer from the accumulation of approximation errors along the predicted trajectory, typically caused by the failure to capture fine-scale details. In this work, we design a Commutator Memory Neural Operator that identifies fine-scale dynamical details by commuting two operations and leverages these details to enhance the neural operator's capability in capturing fine-scale features over long time horizons. Specifically, we identify a performance gap between two operations: downsampling the high-resolution field before rollout prediction versus performing rollout prediction before downsampling. We observe that fine-scale dynamical details are often encoded in this gap. By commuting these two operations, the fine-scale details removed during downsampling can be captured. Furthermore, we employ a memory module to store these fine-scale features along the trajectory and retrieve them during rollout, generating spatially adaptive corrections that enhance long-horizon fidelity. Empirical results across five systems demonstrate that CoMNO improves prediction accuracy and long-horizon rollout stability.
2611.32274.comment: In preparing an earlier version of this manuscript under time pressure, we did not adequately verify all reported experimental results. In this preprint, we correct the numerical reporting errors we identified and update the affected analyses
2611.32274.title: CoMNO: Commutator Memory Neural Operators for Long-Horizon PDE Prediction

2611.32314.abstract: The rapid growth of the Internet of Things (IoT) has increased networked systems' exposure to cyber threats, making Network Intrusion Detection Systems (NIDSs) essential for securing heterogeneous environments. While Deep Learning (DL) has shown strong performance in traffic analysis, Quantum Machine Learning (QML) has recently gained attention as an alternative approach to learn complex traffic patterns. We assess QML's practical applicability to intrusion detection in heterogeneous IoT scenarios. We present a hybrid quantum-classical NIDS and evaluate it on three recent IoT security datasets, under operationally relevant conditions. Beyond detection accuracy, we compare QML with a classical DL baseline across five operational perspectives: (i) performance under data scarcity, (ii) transferability through cross-domain evaluation, (iii) resilience to temporal constraints, (iv) robustness to quantum non-idealities across multiple noisy backends, and (v) prediction trustworthiness through calibration analysis. Experiments on binary and multiclass misuse detection show that DL generally outperforms QML under ideal and noisy conditions. However, QML remains competitive in data-scarcity and domain-shift scenarios and can outperform the DL baseline under temporal constraints.
2611.32314.title: Operationalizing Quantum Machine Learning for IoT Network Intrusion Detection

2611.32459.abstract: Noise in quantum devices remains a major challenge for reliable quantum simulations, making quantum error mitigation an important tool for improving their accuracy. Machine learning-based quantum error mitigation (ML-QEM) provides a useful approach, but its performance depends on the training datasets and may produce reconstructed quantum states that are not physically valid. In this work, we introduce an ML-QEM framework that uses residual learning with convex projection to ensure that reconstructed density matrices satisfy physically valid density matrices. We study the effect of different training datasets and regression models using Haar-random and variational quantum eigensolver (VQE) ansatz states. We compare the proposed approach with conventional ML-QEM, readout error mitigation, and zero-noise extrapolation. The method is tested on IBM quantum hardware for three- and four-qubit simulations of the bound $Λ$-deuteron and $Λ$-$α$ hypernuclear systems, respectively. For the three-qubit system, ridge regression trained on VQE-ansatz states gives a ground-state energy of -0.134 MeV, close to the ideal value of -0.135 MeV, with a state fidelity of 0.999. For four-qubit system, kernel ridge regression gives ground-state energies of -3.014 and -3.045 MeV, with corresponding state fidelities of 0.995 and 0.998. These results show that physically constrained reconstruction, along with the choice of training datasets and regression models, can improve ML-QEM performance for the quantum simulations studied in this work.
2611.32459.title: Machine Learning-Based Quantum Error Mitigation for Bound-State Simulations

2611.32505.abstract: This study integrates satellite remote sensing, groundwater monitoring, and machine learning to map leached-metal-associated hazards at four coal combustion residual (CCR) sites in Virginia, USA. Constituent-specific groundwater concentrations were expressed as Hazard Quotients (HQ) and combined into a composite Hazard Index (HI). Predictors included Sentinel-2 vegetation indices, biophysical parameters, and spatiotemporal metrics (2019-2025), alongside soil, climate, hydrology, topography, and land cover. Six supervised classifiers were evaluated using spatially separated test blocks, feature-set ablation, and leave-one-site-out testing. Higher HQ coincided with lower vegetation indices in 24 of 33 metal-site combinations near monitoring wells (sign test p = 0.007). Well HI was negatively correlated with CIRE and canopy chlorophyll content at three sites (Spearman rho as low as -0.71). Random Forest achieved within-site HI classification accuracies of 0.768-0.924 and higher-HI-class recall of 0.965-0.999. For 34 constituent-site combinations, HQ classification accuracies ranged from 0.775 to 0.989. Environmental covariates generally contributed more predictive information than vegetation features. Removing vegetation predictors did not reduce performance, and distance to the CCR unit alone performed best at one site. Zero-shot cross-site accuracy declined to 0.734-0.749, no better than the majority-class baseline. These findings demonstrate the potential of integrating satellite observations and environmental data with groundwater measurements for site-calibrated spatial hazard screening. The framework identifies indirect environmental associations rather than directly detecting dissolved metals, highlighting the importance of local calibration and independent validation.
2611.32505.title: An Integrated Remote Sensing and Machine Learning Framework for Mapping Hazard Associated with Leached Metals

2611.32518.abstract: Open-vocabulary semantic segmentation (OVSS) enables flexible, text-driven mapping of remote sensing (RS) imagery beyond predefined categories. Despite advances in segmentation foundation models, RS-OVSS remains constrained by the scarcity of large-scale, semantically diverse datasets with accurate pixel-level annotations. Meanwhile, existing RS datasets contain abundant scene- and object-level annotations that offer valuable semantic information but lack precise pixel-wise supervision. To exploit these complementary sources, we propose HS-OVSeg, a unified training framework that integrates heterogeneous scene-, object-, and pixel-level supervision for RS-OVSS. Specifically, we generate pixel-wise pseudo-labels using SAM3, conditioned on scene-level class names and object-level class names with bounding boxes. Combined with ground-truth semantic masks, these pseudo-labels enable joint training across all three annotation granularities through LoRA-based fine-tuning of SAM3. Our unified training spans 20 RS datasets, including 3 scene classification, 4 object detection, and 13 semantic segmentation datasets, with 1,000 images from the 7 classification and detection datasets manually annotated for pixel-level evaluation. HS-OVSeg substantially outperforms existing RS-OVSS models across both the 20 training-source and 5 held-out datasets, demonstrating strong multi-granularity segmentation capabilities under heterogeneous supervision. The code will be publicly available upon publication.
2611.32518.title: HS-OVSeg: Multi-Granularity Open-Vocabulary Semantic Segmentation in Remote Sensing via Heterogeneous Supervision

2611.32739.abstract: We report a step change in what inelastic neutron scattering (INS) can reveal, by combining machine-learned interatomic potentials (MLIPs) with deliberate deuteration of the sample. INS's prowess in charting framework and guest motions within porous materials during in situ dosing has historically had one caveat: costly density-functional-theory calculations are a major bottleneck in the speed and depth of analysis. We show that rapid frontier MLIPs remove this bottleneck on both counts, keeping pace with the experiment while bringing a new level of insight. Deuterating the linkers of ZIF-8 pries apart bands that overlap in the hydrogenous framework, and we test four MLIPs against eight stages of nitrogen dosing at 77 K. On loading, a previously unobserved band appears at 270 cm^-1 and grows gradually through the dosing series. The simulations trace it to single N2 molecules threaded end-on through four-ring windows, each turning its ring of linkers and propping the window open, and unbiased dynamics catch molecules threading into the windows on their own, finding a free-energy trap that crowding stabilizes. This is the first vibrational signature of the threaded state and, crucially, its intensity directly counts the threading over the slow, macroscopic timescale of gas uptake, in situ. More broadly, the simulations explain how each framework band responds to its guests, establishing MLIP-assisted inelastic neutron scattering as a route to mechanism, not just assignment.
2611.32739.comment: 34 pages, 5 figures; Supporting Information (19 figures) included; Movie S1 as an ancillary file
2611.32739.title: Neutron Spectroscopy Transformed: Deuterated ZIF-8 and Machine-Learned Potentials Catch Nitrogen Threading Its Gates

2611.32774.abstract: Physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) enable undiscounted Hamilton-Jacobi (HJ) reachability analysis for high-dimensional systems, but their performance can be sensitive to hyperparameter choices and the underlying system dynamics. We introduce Contract2Reach, which recasts undiscounted finite-horizon reachability as a sequence of contractive fixed-point problems solved by backward time marching. Our formulation combines discretized temporal and spatial derivatives to construct a contractive mapping without introducing a discount factor. Under standard assumptions, we prove that the exact scheme converges to the unique viscosity solution as both the temporal and spatial step sizes tend to zero. Unlike PINNs, our training fits rollout-based value targets via a single regression, without backpropagating through spatial value gradients. In the neural implementation, adaptive zero-level-set sampling and conservative target combination address high-dimensional sample sparsity and false positives, respectively. Experiments on a parameterized vertical drone, a 13D quadrotor, and a 40D publisher-subscriber system show competitive performance against PINNs-based baselines. Boundary evaluations on the vertical drone and publisher-subscriber systems demonstrate improved fidelity and reduced learning-rate sensitivity, revealing errors that volume-based metrics can miss.
2611.32774.title: Contract2Reach: Discretization-Induced Contractive Dynamic Programming for High-Dimensional Hamilton-Jacobi Reachability

2611.32818.abstract: Viscoelastic flow past two side-by-side microcylinders has been shown to exhibit geometry-dependent transitions among symmetric, converging, diverging, and asymmetric-diverging flow states, together with regions of bistability and tristability. Here, we develop a data-driven framework for learning a two-dimensional, parameter-dependent normal form for this bifurcation structure from sparse measurements of stable flow states. We use the flow asymmetry parameters $I'$ and $I''$ as state variables, with the gap ratio $G$ and Weissenberg number $Wi$ as control parameters. In the absence of trajectory data, the measured steady states are enforced as stable equilibria of the learned vector field through equilibrium and local-stability constraints. We examine both polynomial and neural-network representations of the associated normal form and incorporate the physical reflection symmetry directly into the model. The resulting models recover the main geometry-dependent transitions and the overall structure of the experimental phase diagram. To reduce additional stable equilibria that are not constrained by the measurements, we introduce an iterative negative-sample procedure that refines the predicted equilibrium structure. Combining equilibrium data, local stability, physical symmetry, and negative samples yields the closest agreement with the experimental phase diagram among the models considered. The remaining discrepancies reflect the limited information available, solely in the form of sparse equilibrium measurements. Overall, the framework aims to showcase a prototypical example of both the potential and the limitations of inferring nonlinear flow dynamics from sparse equilibrium measurements and highlight the importance of physical constraints and additional dynamical information for reconstructing complex bifurcation structures.
2611.32818.title: Data-driven Reduced-order Modeling of a Multistable Viscoelastic Flow

2611.32851.abstract: Machine learning force fields inherit the errors of the electronic-structure methods used to generate their training data, and refining them against experimental measurements provides a direct route beyond this limit. However, such refinement remains difficult for dynamical observables because differentiating chaotic molecular trajectories yields unstable gradients. Here, we introduce PathGrad, which differentiates Langevin path probabilities instead of the trajectories themselves. The resulting gradient estimator is accumulated on the fly from thermal noise and force derivatives, and its variance remains stable as the trajectory length increases. We validated the gradient estimator against finite-difference calculations and used it to fine-tune molten-copper and water potentials against experimental diffusion coefficients together with structural constraints. For water, jointly optimizing diffusion and the oxygen-oxygen radial distribution function also improves the predictions of shear viscosity and rotational relaxation, neither of which is included in the optimization objective. Alignment at a single temperature also improves the apparent activation energies of multiple dynamical observables, bringing their temperature dependences closer to experiments. Moreover, the optimized potential exhibits smaller force errors relative to an independent, higher-level quantum-chemical reference, indicating that alignment with experiments improves the fidelity of the potential energy surface beyond the fitted targets. PathGrad thus establishes a general framework for incorporating experimental observables directly into force field optimizations.
2611.32851.comment: 20 pages, 6 figures; Supplementary Information (15 pages) included
2611.32851.title: Path-probability gradients for optimizing force fields against dynamical observables

2611.32923.abstract: Quantum noise distorts the distribution of circuit measurement outcomes, often leaving enough information to infer the algorithm's correct result. To recover this latent information from the noisy distribution in Shor order finding, we introduce a theory-informed quantum error mitigation method. We model how circuit errors shift, broaden, or weaken peaks in the output distribution. These models guide both the generation of synthetic training data and the design of a Fourier neural operator with a learned gain that attenuates or amplifies higher retained Fourier modes. We score each candidate order by averaging the correlations between its ideal distribution and the distributions measured in three circuit executions. The network adjusts these scores to guide the order estimate and determine the weights of a normalized mixture of the ideal distributions. On 1,351 simulated test cases for general modular exponentiation, held out by circuit configuration, exact order recovery rises from 19% to 34%, and the median Jensen-Shannon divergence from the ideal distribution falls by 50%, from 0.64 to 0.32. On 101 Mersenne rotation circuits executed across five IBM quantum processors, a separate model trained and calibrated in simulation increases the number of correct order estimates from 35 to 53. Algorithmic structure can remain recoverable even when noise makes it barely visible.
2611.32923.comment: 18 pages, 10 figures, 1 table. Revised version of the published article
2611.32923.title: Theory-Informed Quantum Error Mitigation for Shor Order Finding with Fourier Neural Operators

2611.33097.abstract: Hemocytes, the macrophages of Drosophila, disperse through the embryo and then patrol its tissues, moving along basement membranes that they help to build. Because the persistence (H) and amplitude (D) of hemocyte motion vary along each track, it is difficult to describe how movement changes during development and how it depends on basement membrane composition. We analysed trajectories, obtained by selective plane illumination microscopy, of hemocytes in control embryos and in embryos deficient in the basement membrane components laminin (LanB1-deficient) or collagen IV (collagen-deficient). A physics-informed neural network estimates H and D in short windows, each with a calibrated uncertainty. From them we construct an effective diffusivity Deff, defined for any anomalous diffusion as the diffusivity of the unpredictable part of the motion. Its error is uncorrelated with that of H and acts as an effective temperature. Cells decelerate during development by cooling (falling Deff) and forgetting (falling H). Control cells cool gradually while staying persistent. LanB1-deficient cells cool further, forget, lose the coupling between speed and persistence and become nearly Brownian. Collagen-deficient cells cool but keep most of their persistence. Hemocyte movement thus resembles an annealed search, in which laminin, rather than collagen IV, keeps patrolling cells persistent.
2611.33097.title: From dispersal to patrol: the extracellular matrix shapes an annealing-like search by Drosophila embryonic macrophages

2611.33150.abstract: We propose Boseformer, a universal attention-based neural-network architecture for representing the wavefunctions of particles with bosonic quantum statistics, including superfluid and crystal phases. The model is trained to generate the wavefunction as a function of a Hamiltonian parameter across the quantum phase transition between these phases. Once trained with variational Monte Carlo optimization, it can serve as a foundation model describing the phase transition without the need to retrain it for individual parameter values. We demonstrate our method on a system of two-dimensional bosons with $1/r^3$ repulsive interaction.
2611.33150.title: Parametric neural-network wavefunctions across a bosonic phase transition
